html: The Plains Miwok were a people of the lower Sacramento and San Joaquin rivers and the Delta in California's Central Valley, part of the larger Miwok family that also included the Sierra Miwok of the foothills, such as the Central Sierra Miwok. They lived in villages along the rivers and sloughs, eating acorns, salmon, seeds and tule elk. From about 1810 many were drawn or taken into the Spanish missions near San Francisco Bay, especially Mission San José. A malaria epidemic in 1833 killed many of the valley peoples, and the Gold Rush of 1848 overran the rest. Their northern neighbours were the Nisenan, and descendants today belong to the Wilton Rancheria and other bands.
